title: The envsubst wrapper contract passes when it cannot find the invocation it is contracted to check
discoveredBy: BUG-061-011 regression phase; independently re-verified by the operator and again by bubbles.bug at HEAD 4895d446

executionHistory.summary: Filed BUG-061-013 at HEAD 4895d446. NO FIX IMPLEMENTED and no source file touched; every DoD item in scopes.md and every delivery item in uservalidation.md is unchecked. The defect was reported by the BUG-061-011 regression phase and by the operator, and was RE-VERIFIED here rather than restated: (1) `grep -nE '^\s*go\s+test\b' scripts/runtime/go-integration.sh` exits 1 with no output, which is the exact pattern compiled at internal/deploy/envsubst_wrapper_contract_test.go:82; (2) `grep -n 'go test'` on the same file returns line 76 `if ! go test "${go_test_args[@]}" 2>&1 | tee "$gate_output_file"; then`, whose `if ! ` prefix defeats the `^\s*` anchor; (3) the green subtest was CONFIRMED IN THIS SESSION rather than taken on report — `./smackerel.sh test unit --go --go-run 'TestEnvsubstWrapperContract' --verbose` exits 0 with a literal `--- PASS: TestEnvsubstWrapperContract_LiveWrappers/go-integration.sh (0.00s)` line and `ok github.com/smackerel/smackerel/internal/deploy 0.115s`. No drift from the reported observations was found. ROOT CAUSE, located in source: two composing mistakes. Cause 1 — envsubstGoTestRE is lexical and anchored, so it encodes a syntax assumption; its own comment concedes only that 'Whitespace-leading is OK', which is false for `if`, `if !`, `&&`, `||`, pipelines, `env VAR=x`, or `timeout N`. Cause 2 — line 108's `goTestIdx != nil &&` short-circuit reads absence as compliance, so a zero match returns nil. The function is internally inconsistent: the source-line locator (92-96) and the call locator (98-101) both ERROR on absence; only the go-test locator passes. The charitable reading of `!= nil` ('nothing to order against') is sound only if the locator is complete; because it is anchored, zero-match actually means 'runs go test in a form I do not recognise'. envsubstTrackedWrappers (lines 55-60) is itself the disproof — membership asserts the wrapper runs go test, so a tracked wrapper with zero matches is self-contradictory and must fail. ORIGIN traced by execution: c7667d99 ('feat(stage-1): eval-gate lane wiring…', the BUG-061-011 fix) changed the file by 74 insertions / 2 deletions; at c7667d99^ line 55 read `go test "${go_test_args[@]}"` and MATCHED. BLAST RADIUS measured: go-integration.sh is the ONLY wrapper currently blind — go-unit.sh (line 67), go-e2e.sh (line 89) and go-stress.sh (line 50) all still match — but all four share the zero-match branch, so the latent radius is all four (recorded in report.md as an inference, not an observation). WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT: all three adversarial fixtures (lines 184, 204, 224) write `go test ./...` bare and at line start, so the regex matches in every fixture the suite owns and the zero-match branch has no test at all. FIX DIRECTIONS with tradeoffs are in design.md; PRIMARY is (a) make zero-match a hard failure, chosen because it is the only option that fixes the class rather than the instance — (b) widening the regex and (c) semantic parsing both improve the locator's reach, and neither changes what happens when the locator is out of reach, which is the actual defect. (a) and (b) must land together: (a) alone leaves the lane RED on a true finding, (b) alone turns it green while the silent-pass hole stays open. SEVERITY IS DELIBERATELY NOT INFLATED: ensure_envsubst runs at line 14 and go test at line 76, so the ordering the contract protects genuinely holds and no user-facing behaviour is asserted broken. The doubled-pipe alternative precedes the single pipe, which LOOKS load-bearing and is not, because Go's regexp is RE2 and finds a match if any alternative matches; a warning about a non-hazard would mislead the next reader, which is the failure this pass exists to prevent. Those are NOT interchangeable — measured on a blank-line-before-token shape they report offsets 45 vs 46, because \s includes newline and can begin a match at an earlier blank line, and offsets are exactly what this function's ordering comparisons consume. It still cannot cause harm: substituting \s for the horizontal-whitespace class in ALL THREE matchers changes 0 of 11 verdicts across the 5 real fixtures, 2 probes built specifically to trigger the offset shift, and all 4 live wrappers. The zero is STRUCTURAL, not luck — \s* can only extend a match start backward through contiguous whitespace, and every offset pair the function compares (callIdx vs srcIdx, goTestIdx vs callIdx) is separated by a line of non-whitespace text it cannot span, so the pull-back is bounded and can never cross the other token's line. The comment's operative claim ('anchors to line start so the rationale comment above does NOT match') is true of both forms. Editing a hardened, adversarially-tested contract file to correct an inert paraphrase is churn, so the analysis is recorded for its owner instead. DETERMINISM: the nondeterminism sweep over the contract test returns EMPTY for map iteration, os.ReadDir, filepath.Walk, filepath.Glob, time.Now, math/rand and t.Parallel, so the only iteration is the fixed envsubstTrackedWrappers slice and subtest order is declaration order, as the transcript confirms. Working-directory independence turns on one fact that was checked rather than assumed: envsubstWrapperRepoRoot derives the root from runtime.Caller(0) plus two parents, which is a COMPILE-time path, so a trimmed build would make it module-relative and therefore CWD-resolved. 'git grep trimpath' exits 1 (genuinely absent) and 'grep -rnE go-test-c' over scripts/ exits 1, so the path is absolute AND no wrapper builds a detached binary that could desync compile-time from run-time paths. An earlier form of the trimpath check returned exit 2, which is grep's ERROR code and not no-match (that is 1) because a non-existent glob poisoned the argument list; it was re-run against paths that exist, and accepting the first result would have reproduced this packet's own silent-pass class inside its evidence. The exec-bit assertion is reproducible because the mode is VERSIONED, not filesystem-derived: git ls-files -s reports 100755 for _ensure_envsubst.sh. go-unit.sh:63 appends -count=1 with the selector, so the Go test cache cannot replay a stale pass. FAILURE MODE: the zero-match branch is a pure in-memory regex over an already-read byte slice with no I/O, no network, no loop and no sleep, so it cannot hang; it fails on the first unlocatable wrapper. Its message is actionable and correctly DIRECTED, saying the wrapper is not necessarily wrong and must not be rewritten, and naming envsubstGoTestRE as the remediation target, which matters because the tempting wrong fix is editing a correct wrapper until a blind matcher matches it. That is not asserted but EXECUTED: AdversarialRejectsUnlocatableInvocation asserts the message contains both 'could not LOCATE' and 'matcher may need widening' and PASSED, and AdversarialRejectsConditionalCallAfterGoTest demands the ORDERING error specifically, obtainable only if the widened matcher bound the real 'if ! go test | tee' line, and PASSED. COST: internal/deploy completes in 0.025s, the FLOOR of the 0.025-0.075s band from prior lanes, over 12799 bytes across the four tracked wrappers, with all three patterns as package-level regexp.MustCompile vars so they compile once per binary rather than per wrapper. Catastrophic backtracking CANNOT OCCUR here rather than being unlikely: Go's regexp is RE2-based and documented to run in time linear in input size, simulating an NFA without backtracking, so the nested quantifier that would be a genuine ReDoS hazard in a PCRE-family engine is linear here; the claim is stated as impossibility by construction, not as a warning about a hazard that cannot arise. LANES: the instability sweep over this packet's 104KB report.md, which carries the integration (10252 lines, exit 0) and e2e (4528 lines, exit 0) transcripts, returns 0 for retry, retrying, timed out, unhealthy, restarting, flaky, panic and DATA RACE, with 3 benign 'health' readiness references; those long lanes were deliberately NOT re-run. The window was widened to 280 and the re-run shows ELEVEN named --- PASS lines, seven top-level plus four LiveWrappers subtests, including both fixtures this packet added. The decisive discriminator is an ABSENCE: 'ok internal/deploy 0.025s' carries NO '[no tests to run]' suffix while its immediate neighbours internal/db 0.020s and internal/digest 0.028s both do, so a zero-match run would have rendered internal/deploy exactly like its neighbours. DETERMINISM CAVEAT recorded for later phases: run1 sha256 9053b2a8 and run2 sha256 976c1d16 differ while both are exit 0, 540 lines, with an identical eleven-PASS set, because per-package timing floats and apt-get transfer rates vary; the lane is RESULT-deterministic but not BYTE-deterministic, so evidence-capture --verify against it returns exit 3 on a clean re-run and a mismatch there must not be read as a regression. WHAT THE GUARD PROTECTS, traced rather than assumed: envsubst has exactly ONE call site in the repository, scripts/commands/config.sh:3163, and it uses envsubst ALLOW-LIST form over four named non-secret numeric variables (two scrape intervals, two container ports), so every other token in the template is emitted literally. The unrestricted form that would expand the whole environment is used nowhere. The one secret-bearing artifact, the NATS conf carrying the auth section, is rendered thirty lines earlier by printf at chmod 0600 and never passes through envsubst. The tempting hypothesis that a missing or mis-ordered substitution could leak, blank, or mis-resolve a secret is therefore FALSE here, and saying so plainly is more useful than inventing a hazard. CONSEQUENCE IF THE ORDERING SILENTLY BREAKS is availability and guard integrity, not confidentiality, and that was measured: all 35 test files that shell out to config.sh report ignored_exit_patterns=0, config.sh itself opens with set -euo pipefail, and internal/deploy/alertmanager_bundle_contract_test.go parses the rendered prometheus.yml and requires an alerting.alertmanagers block, so a bad render fails loudly too. No silent-degradation path exists; this contract is a second line of defence over an already-loud failure, and this phase does not claim more for it. The real security story is that go-integration.sh was silently UNGUARDED: the assertion ran, compared nothing, and reported PASS, supplying assurance it had not earned.
